title: The city bike-lane pilot
blurb: Check the controls, measurements, and scope — is there actually a fallacy here?
prompt: Read this municipal transit brief carefully. Flag any logical or statistical flaw, or mark it clean if the reasoning holds up.

segments.label: Claim 1
segments.text: The city installed a protected bike lane on Oak Avenue and tracked weekday traffic for 12 full months before and 12 months after.

segments.label: Claim 2
segments.text: Over the exact same period, planners also monitored Pine Avenue — a nearby commercial street with similar traffic that did not get a bike lane.

segments.label: Claim 3
segments.text: Daily bike trips rose 35% on Oak Avenue versus only 5% on Pine Avenue, suggesting a roughly 30-point gain beyond citywide seasonal trends.

segments.label: Claim 4
segments.text: Local card-payment totals along Oak Avenue stayed flat (+1.2% vs +0.9% on Pine), rather than relying only on informal merchant surveys.

segments.label: Claim 5
segments.text: The pilot supports a net rise in cycling on flat commercial corridors like Oak Avenue, though steeper or suburban roads may behave differently.

conclusion: Verdict: Controlled data supports a real cycling increase on Oak Avenue without measurable harm to local card sales, with scope limits noted.
